label: Features
title: School finance software for fees, receipts and debtor management
description: School, university and bus fee billing, recurring invoice drafts, receipts, debtor balances and optional e-invoicing modules in one institution workspace.
heading: The whole fee journey. One clear workspace.
intro: Bring students, billable units, invoices and receipts into one financial account. Bursara helps your team follow each charge from the day it is raised to the moment its balance is settled.
cardRows: A learner and a responsible payer
cardNote: A connected workflow, from enrolment details to the financial record.

sections.heading: Start with the learner, then the fees.
body: A school finance record begins with a student, but the person paying may be a parent, a guardian or a sponsor. Keep that relationship visible alongside the student’s course and enrolled units.

A course describes the complete programme. Its units describe the parts you price, such as a school year or a university module. This gives your team a consistent starting point when preparing a bill.
points: Student and debtor details together
Courses with fixed-fee or per-credit units
An individual account with invoices and receipts

sections.heading: Prepare first. Post when authorised.
body: Save a draft while you check the learner, fees and payment terms. Authorised users can edit it before posting. A draft does not change account balances or consume a final invoice or receipt number.
Posting has its own permission. The permanent creation reference remains unchanged, while the final document number is assigned only when the financial record is posted.
points: Editable drafts before confirmation
Separate creation and posting permissions
Final numbers assigned on posting

sections.heading: Charge in the way your institution works.
body: Raise the annual fee once and spread its due dates across monthly instalments. Alternatively, prepare an invoice for selected units or receive full payment when issuing the document.
A posted bill records what is owed. Its payment schedule explains when it becomes due. Those are separate questions, and Bursara keeps both visible.
points: Custom fee lines alongside enrolled units
Line discounts and tax amounts where applicable
A printable document with an outstanding balance

sections.heading: Give every payment a place.
body: Record a payment that your institution has already received, identify its payer and apply it to the student’s outstanding fees. A receipt preserves that payment record.

If money is received before you choose a bill, it can remain as unapplied student credit. Financial corrections use separate credit or refund records so that the original posting remains part of the account.
points: Part payments and allocations
Bank, cash, external card and cleared cheque records
Separate records for credits and refunds

sections.heading: Keep the team working within clear boundaries.
body: Each institution has its own workspace. Its administrators create users and choose the actions those users may perform. Platform support staff can enter an institution for authorised assistance.
Local fiscal requirements sit in optional modules. The initial EBS Mauritius module uses sandbox reporting, while the core fee account works independently of it.
points: Institution-specific records and permissions
Visible support access within a client workspace
Separate balances for each transaction currency

sections.heading: Repeat the fee schedule, keep the review.
body: Prepare one-off charges when needed, or set a recurring billing schedule for weekly, monthly, quarterly, four-month, six-month or yearly fees. School tuition, university fees and bus transport can follow different schedules.
Each scheduled run creates an editable invoice draft. An authorised person checks and posts it separately. A schedule does not automatically collect money or post an invoice.
points: Ad-hoc fees alongside repeating charges
Automatic draft creation from a saved template
Separate review and posting permissions

sections.heading: Core finance, optional modules.
body: Use the financial workspace for learners, school fees, university units, bus charges, receipts and debtor follow-up. Optional modules add specific functions without making them dependencies of the core account.

The first available external module is EBS e-invoicing for Mauritius, currently using its test environment. The architecture leaves room for additional country providers and future institution modules. Attendance, timetables and other future modules are not included today.
points: Core financial management works independently
Optional jurisdiction-specific e-invoicing
Additional modules can be developed as needs grow

example.title: An annual fee, without losing the part payments.
example.body: For an illustrative 120,000 annual school bill, a 25,000 payment leaves 95,000 outstanding. The invoice total, amount paid and remaining instalments tell different parts of the same story.

faq: Is Bursara a complete school learning platform?

The application focuses on invoicing, receipting and financial administration. Attendance, check-in and check-out, timetables and broader student management are potential future modules, not application features.
Does it replace my accounting platform?
Bursara maintains the student fee account and financial control records. It does not currently integrate with an accounting platform or claim to replace a complete statutory accounting system.
Can I test the full workflow?
Yes. Use the application with fictional students and simulated payments. The help guide explains how to create a course, enrol a student, post fees and record a receipt.
What does the Mauritius EBS module support?

The optional module uses explicit sandbox preparation and submission. Its current invoice mapper supports undiscounted exempt or 15% service lines; payment-trigger preparation is limited to allocated, zero-tax tuition. Live fiscalisation and fiscal credit notes are not yet available. The help guide explains the workflow and its limits.
Does recurring billing automatically post invoices or take payment?
No. Due schedules automatically create drafts. An authorised user reviews and posts each invoice; payments remain separate records of money actually received.

label: Student billing
title: Student invoicing and unit-based school fee billing
description: Prepare one-off or recurring student fee drafts for tuition, university units and bus transport. Review and post invoices with separate permissions.
heading: Fees that follow your programme.
intro: A school year, a professional course or selected university units. Build the bill around what the learner is enrolled in, then make the payment terms clear from the start.
cardNote: The fee is raised once. Its due dates explain when the balance should be paid.

sections.heading: Separate the course from the billable unit.
body: “High School” can be the overall course, with Years 1, 2, 3 and 4 as its priced units. A degree programme can instead contain named modules, each with its own fee or credit weight.

Enrol the student in the appropriate units before billing them. Choosing an enrolled unit gives the invoice a clear description and a starting price, while a custom line can cover another legitimate charge.
points: Whole programmes with individual priced units
Fixed charges or a price per credit
Clear student and responsible-payer details

sections.heading: Prepare first. Post when authorised.
body: Save a draft while you check the learner, fees and payment terms. Authorised users can edit it before posting. A draft does not change account balances or consume a final invoice or receipt number.
Posting has its own permission. The permanent creation reference remains unchanged, while the final document number is assigned only when the financial record is posted.
points: Editable drafts before confirmation

Final numbers assigned on posting

sections.heading: Bill now. Collect over time.
body: An annual charge does not need to become twelve separate invoices. Raise the full fee and divide its due amount across a monthly schedule. As payments are applied, the student’s balance and remaining due amounts change.

This helps distinguish the total commitment for the year from the amount that is overdue today. Choosing a balance date lets the finance team review the account position at a particular point in time.
points: A single bill with multiple instalment dates
Part payments against the outstanding amount
Remaining balance separate from overdue instalments

sections.heading: Make the document fit the transaction.
body: When fees are owed before payment, post an invoice and collect later. When the full amount is received at the point of issue, use the receive-and-issue workflow to create a settled invoice and its payment record together.
A receipt acknowledges money received. An unpaid invoice records money owed. A combined paid document brings those actions together when that matches the transaction.
points: Bill first and receive payment later
Receive full payment and issue together
Printable documents for review or browser PDF saving

sections.heading: Correct the account with a clear record.
body: Posted fees should tell a consistent story. When an outstanding charge needs reducing, record a credit with an amount, date and reason rather than changing the original total invisibly.

Bursara’s general credit workflow applies to outstanding fees. Documents that have entered fiscal reporting need jurisdiction-specific correction handling, which remains outside Bursara’s core credit workflow.
points: Separate credit entries with an explanation
Original posted bill remains in the account
Totals calculated using the currency’s precision

sections.heading: Repeat the fee schedule, keep the review.

Each scheduled run creates an editable invoice draft. An authorised person checks and posts it separately. A schedule does not automatically collect money or post an invoice.
points: Ad-hoc fees alongside repeating charges

example.title: One learner. Two university units.
example.body: An illustrative biomedical sciences student takes a three-credit Cell Biology unit priced at 250 per credit and a Laboratory Skills unit priced at 400. Their fee invoice brings the selected charges together.

faq: Can I charge by school year and by individual university module?
Yes. Use a whole programme as the course and create the priced years or modules as units. A unit can have a fixed fee or a price multiplied by its credit weight.
Does Bursara automatically generate every future invoice?
The module supports choosing a service period and creating an instalment schedule when posting a bill. It does not currently generate future invoices automatically on a recurring schedule.
Can I send invoices by email from Bursara?
The workflow provides on-screen and printable documents. Automated document email delivery is not part of the application.

label: Receipts & payments
title: School payment receipts and student fee allocations
description: Record school fee payments, issue receipts and allocate part payments to student invoices. Track unapplied credit and separate financial corrections.
heading: Every payment, clearly accounted for.
intro: Know who paid, how much arrived and which fees it settled. Record the money your institution has received, then give the payment a clear place in the student’s account.
cardNote: Bursara records a payment already received. It does not process a bank transfer or charge a card.

sections.heading: Record the receipt of money.
body: Create a payment with its student, payer, amount, currency, received date and method. Add the bank, cash-office or external payment reference that helps your team recognise the transaction later.
The application records confirmed bank transfers, cash, external card payments and cleared cheques. It does not initiate transfers, collect card details or confirm a bank settlement on your behalf.
A payment can be saved and edited as a draft. Its receipt number, financial journal and effect on available funds begin only when an authorised user posts it.
points: A numbered receipt for each payment record
The payer and student remain connected
A transaction date and optional external reference

sections.heading: Apply the payment to the right fees.
body: A student may have several open bills. Choose the invoices the payment should settle and enter the amount applied to each. A part payment can reduce a balance without marking the whole fee as paid.
Allocations keep the received money separate from the charges it settles. The amount applied cannot exceed the payment available or the outstanding bill balance.
points: Allocate across a student’s outstanding bills
See a bill’s paid amount and remaining balance
Keep other students’ accounts separate

sections.heading: Recognise advances and unused credit.
body: Sometimes money arrives before you decide which bill it should settle. Record it as unapplied student credit instead of forcing an allocation to an unrelated invoice.
An unused balance is visible alongside the receipt. Where a refund is appropriate, the application provides a separate refund record for unapplied money, with a date and reason.
points: Payment received independently of an invoice
Available credit distinguished from already-applied money
Refund records preserve the original receipt

sections.heading: Give the payer a readable document.
body: Open the receipt to inspect the amount received, its method and the invoice allocations. The document shows the financial effect of the payment instead of simply repeating a bank reference.

Print the receipt or save it as PDF using the browser. If the institution receives full payment as it raises a charge, its combined workflow can also produce a paid invoice and the matching receipt record.
points: Readable payment and allocation details
Separate receipt and invoice references
Print layouts designed for the document

example.title: A payment larger than today’s allocation.
example.body: In this example, an institution receives 30,000 and applies 25,000 to annual tuition. The remaining 5,000 stays visible as unapplied student credit rather than being counted as payment of another charge.

faq: Does Bursara take online card payments?
No. The application records a card payment that has already been processed externally. It does not collect card details or charge the payer.
Can a parent pay only part of an invoice?
Yes. Record the amount actually received and apply that amount to the student’s bill. The unpaid remainder stays outstanding.
Can I refund a payment already applied to tuition?
Bursara’s refund workflow is limited to unapplied money. It does not directly reverse a settled fee allocation or provide a complete paid-invoice reversal workflow.

label: Debtor management
title: School fee debtor management and outstanding student balances
description: Review unpaid school fees, overdue instalments and student debtor balances by date and currency. Follow each account back to its invoices and receipts.
heading: See the balance. Understand what is due.
intro: A large annual balance is not always a late payment. Bursara separates the fee still outstanding from the instalments already overdue, so your team can review each student’s position with context.
cardNote: Review the remaining commitment and the due schedule together.

sections.heading: Distinguish outstanding from overdue.
body: Outstanding fees are charges that have not yet been settled by payments or credits. Some of that balance may be payable in future months. Overdue amounts relate to instalments that fell due before the chosen balance date.
Keeping the two figures separate supports a more accurate conversation with the parent, student or sponsor responsible for payment.
points: Whole invoice balances remain visible
Monthly due dates provide the payment context
The responsible payer is linked to the student

sections.heading: Review the account at a chosen date.
body: Select a balance date to inspect the financial position rather than relying only on today’s total. Payment and credit dates matter when understanding what was outstanding at an earlier point.
This is useful when a finance administrator is reviewing a period, preparing a collection list or explaining why an account was overdue before a later payment arrived.
points: A date-based view of outstanding accounts
Separate currency selection for clearer totals
Direct links from the debtor list to source documents

sections.heading: Follow the figures back to the documents.
body: A balance is easier to resolve when the underlying records are close at hand. Open the invoice to review charges and instalments, or open the student account to see the learner’s bills and receipts together.
Payments show the amount received and how it was allocated. Credits show the reduction and its reason. Your team can explain the account through its actual entries.
points: Invoice totals, payments and remaining balances
Separate financial correction records
A learner-centred account history

sections.heading: Take a clear list into the next conversation.
body: Use the debtor view to identify open accounts and the reporting export to work with invoice balances outside the application. Currency amounts remain separate rather than being added together as if they were the same money.
The application helps your team review and record the collection process. It does not currently send automated reminder campaigns, debt collection notices or payment-demand emails.
points: On-screen debtor review
CSV export of invoice balance information
Human-led follow-up with the responsible payer

example.title: Paid ahead of the next instalment.
example.body: A 120,000 invoice has twelve 10,000 monthly instalments beginning at the end of January. A 25,000 payment received in February covers the first two instalments and part of the third. Before the third instalment is due, 95,000 can remain outstanding without being overdue.

faq: Does every unpaid fee appear as overdue?
No. A future instalment can remain outstanding without being overdue. Bursara uses the due schedule and selected balance date to distinguish the two.
Does it automatically email payment reminders?
No. Automated reminder delivery is outside the application. Your team reviews the debtor list and handles communication with the payer.
Can I combine and balances in one total?
The account views keep transaction currencies separate. Selecting a currency avoids presenting unrelated amounts as a single total.

label: Multiple currencies
title: Multi-currency student billing and school payment records
description: Bill and record student fee payments in supported currencies, preserve currency precision and view balances separately in Bursara.
heading: Different currencies. The same clear account.
intro: An international learner, an overseas sponsor or a course priced in another currency should still have a readable fee account. Bursara keeps each transaction’s currency visible from bill to receipt.
cardNote: The institution’s functional currency is set when its workspace is created.

sections.heading: Price and bill in the right currency.
body: Choose a currency for each priced unit and record the currency of the invoice you raise. A university programme can use a different fee currency from the institution’s everyday functional currency.
The currency belongs to the transaction, not just the visual formatting. Invoices and receipts retain it so that the payer and finance team can identify what was actually charged or received.
points: A choice of supported transaction currencies
Currency retained on invoices and receipts
Clear student balances for each currency

sections.heading: Respect the currency’s decimal precision.
body: Currencies do not all use the same number of decimal places. Bursara respects the precision of the selected currency when calculating charges, receipts and allocations.
Bursara calculates charges, discounts, taxes and allocations with the supported currency’s precision, and preserves the posted totals as the financial record.
points: Whole-unit, two-decimal and three-decimal amount handling
Consistently calculated invoice totals
Exact allocation amounts and instalment remainders

sections.heading: Record the exchange rate deliberately.
body: When a transaction uses a foreign currency, enter its rate to the institution’s functional currency. The application does not fetch a live market rate automatically. The person posting the transaction must choose the appropriate rate.
For a payment applied across currencies, record both the amount settled on the invoice and the amount consumed from the receipt. These are explicit values, not an assumed one-to-one allocation.
points: An entered functional-currency exchange rate
Explicit invoice and payment amounts for cross-currency allocation
Financial control entries capture the conversion effect

sections.heading: Keep reports readable.
body: The overview, debtor view and reports distinguish each transaction currency. Balances in different currencies are not simply added together. Select the currency you want to review and follow its invoices and receipts.
This supports an international fee operation while retaining the context needed to explain the student account. Local fiscal reporting remains a separate jurisdiction-specific concern.
points: Per-currency billed and outstanding amounts
Payment amounts shown in the received currency
Optional fiscal modules independent of the core account

example.title: One settlement, two clearly recorded amounts.
example.body: When the receipt and invoice use different currencies, record the amount settled on the invoice and the amount used from the payment separately. Keep the agreed exchange rate with the transaction.

faq: Can an institution use more than one currency?
Yes. Select from the supported currencies in the application. Invoices, receipts and balances keep their currency. Currency support does not mean every jurisdiction’s fiscal rules are implemented.
Are exchange rates updated automatically?
No. Enter the rate to the institution’s functional currency when posting a foreign-currency transaction. Bursara does not currently provide a live foreign-exchange feed.
Does multi-currency support include international tax compliance?
No. Currency handling is part of the core account. E-invoicing and other local requirements belong in separate jurisdiction modules; the initial Mauritius EBS module is sandbox-only in Bursara.

intro: The names of the programmes may change, but the finance office still needs to know what was charged, who is responsible and what remains unpaid. Bursara starts with those common questions.

Raise the appropriate year’s fee and record an instalment schedule. The finance team can then track the full annual commitment without treating every future monthly amount as late.

A parent or guardian as the responsible payer
An account combining invoices and receipts

Use a fixed fee for a unit or a per-credit price where that fits the programme. Enrol the learner in the units they are taking, then create a bill for the relevant components.

Fixed or per-credit pricing
Student, guardian or sponsor debtor details

A visible support workspace context

Those wider operations can be considered as later modules. The current evaluation is about getting the core financial journey clear: programme, charge, payment and outstanding account.
points: A focused fee administration workflow
Optional local e-invoicing modules
An application designed for testing with fictional data

example.title: Choose the unit that describes the charge.
example.body: The same structure can describe several educational settings without making every institution behave like a university. The important step is deciding which part of a programme carries a price.

faq: Can different schools share the same user workspace?
Each institution has its own workspace and users. Platform support staff have separate tools for entering a client institution when providing authorised assistance.
Is Bursara also a learning management system?
No. Teaching content, classroom allocation and coursework management are outside the current financial application.
Can I evaluate the model before adding a real school?

Yes. Use synthetic records in the protected demonstration institution, or ask the team about a separate evaluation workspace. Real student and financial data should not be entered during application testing.

Students can be enrolled in the relevant units of their course, and the finance user can bill selected enrolled units. It is a fee structure, not a full academic registration or timetable system.

Does Bursara connect to our existing accounting software?

label: About Bursara
title: About Bursara school finance software by Streak Technologies Ltd
description: Meet Bursara, the school billing and receipting product by Streak Technologies Ltd, focused on financial clarity for learning institutions.
heading: Financial clarity. More room to learn.
intro: Bursara is a product of Streak Technologies Ltd. We are building a considered workspace for the people who manage fees, record payments and keep educational accounts understandable.
cardNote: A focused financial foundation for schools, colleges and other learning institutions.

sections.heading: Designed around the finance office.
body: Education administration is broad. The person receiving school fees often needs something more focused than classroom allocation or coursework tools: a clear answer to what was charged, what has been paid and what is still outstanding.
Bursara begins there. Its core model connects learners and payers to priced course units, invoices, receipts and the remaining financial account.
points: A financial workflow built around learning institutions
Plain documents and readable ledger views
A consistent account from bill to payment

sections.heading: A practical application, open to careful testing.
body: The current release is an application for evaluating the end-to-end financial journey. Testers can work with synthetic records, inspect printed documents and report where a workflow needs improving.

It is not ready for live school operations, statutory reporting or real student data. Demonstration records may be reset as the product develops. The next steps should follow evidence from testing rather than claims about features that do not yet exist.
points: Use fictional learner and financial records
Evaluate ordinary finance tasks from start to finish
Share specific steps and expected outcomes when reporting a problem

sections.heading: Local requirements belong in local modules.
body: The core account should remain useful across learning institutions in different countries. Currency handling and financial records sit at the centre, while local e-invoicing belongs behind a jurisdiction-specific module.

The first such module is EBS Mauritius. In the application it targets sandbox reporting and requires separate configuration and explicit submission. This is a starting point for local integrations, not a claim of worldwide fiscal compliance.
points: Core fee management independent of EBS
Optional Mauritius sandbox integration
Room for future jurisdiction-specific providers

example.body: A charge, a receipt and a remaining balance should fit together in a way a finance user and payer can understand. That is the practical measure behind Bursara’s billing and receipting work.

faq: Who is Bursara for?
Bursara is being developed for schools, academies, colleges and training providers that need a focused student invoicing, receipting and financial administration workflow.
Who provides Bursara?
Bursara is a product of Streak Technologies Ltd. You can contact the team at support@streaktechnologies.com or visit streaktechnologies.com.
Can we discuss our institution’s requirements?
Yes. Use the contact page to reach the team. when using the demonstration, use fictional records rather than sending personal student information or live financial documents.
